//: Configuration for a Tiny Tapeout micro tile container on sky130A:
a 1x1 project (161.00 x 111.52 um) holding four 70.38 x 51.68 um micro tiles.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
The micro tiles sit in the four corners of the tile, with their signal pins facing a
20.24 um wide channel in the middle (the right column is mirrored). Their left, right and
bottom margins overlap the margins of the container. The mux logic goes in the channel
and in the row above the micro tiles, below the pins of the container.
Keep the container's standard cells (and their met1 rails) clear of the micro tiles.
The vertical halo also removes the row right above the micro tiles.
Power: the micro tiles have horizontal met3 power stripes. The container's vertical met4
stripes run over the micro tiles; setting PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER to met3 makes the macro
grid add via3 arrays wherever a met4 stripe crosses a met3 stripe of the same net.
(The container itself has no horizontal stripes: FP_PDN_MULTILAYER is off.)
Vertical met4 stripes: VPWR at x = 10.12, 32.20, ... 142.60 and VGND at x = 21.16, 43.24,
... 153.64. Every micro tile gets three stripes of each net, and the channel between them
one of each. The stripes sit halfway between the met4 pins at the top of the tile.
The micro tiles own met1, met2 and met3 inside their area, except for the 1 um strip
along the channel where their signal pins are. met4 over the micro tiles stays available.
LVS on a layout extracted from the final GDS, transistors of the micro tiles included,
against the netlist of the container plus the powered netlists of the micro tiles.
Save some time
Don't put clock buffers on the outputs
Reduce wasted space
Absolute die size
Clock
Don't generate power rings
MAGIC_DEF_LABELS may cause issues with LVS
Only export pin area in LEF (without any connected nets)
